research_analysis.exact_observed_hook: No speech. On-screen text: "3D printing until I'm a millionaire 💸 part 15"
research_analysis.visual_hook: A young man in a black hoodie standing in a workshop filled with rows of 3D printers, throwing his fists in the air.
research_analysis.narrative_structure: Series title with a part number (0-2s). Work shown as a string of small events, each tagged with a pop-up gain (+$39.99) or loss (-$120) and a matching sound (2-9s). Day summary in text ("Today we had 72 orders"). A named sidekick gets two captions ("Juan packaged them...", "Happy Juan"). Errand ("Post office time"). End card with two numbers: Today's Total and Series Total. 14 shots in 37 seconds, no speech, upbeat music.
research_analysis.viral_mechanism: The title promises a finish line and the part number proves it is ongoing, so the end card is a score update the viewer waits for. Each pop-up is a tiny win or loss, which gives the eye something to track every 2 to 3 seconds without a word spoken.
research_analysis.observed_evidence: 6.8M views on a 14.1K-subscriber channel, breakout score 513. It is part 15, so the format had been repeated at least 14 times before this one. 37 seconds, 14 shots, zero dialogue, sound effects on every pop-up, one loss shown among the gains.
research_analysis.performance_hypothesis: Hypothesis: the Series Total turns a single video into a reason to subscribe, because the number is unfinished. The one visible loss (-$120) is what makes the gains believable. Viewers comment on the running number and on the sidekick.
research_analysis.why_this_format_fits_alex: It is silent and text-driven like his two largest Reels, and it gives his 100K goal a recurring scoreboard. An agency has no product to stack, so the tally has to count things that are visible on a phone: reels posted, views, followers. He already posts 4 to 10 Trial Reels a day, so the raw material exists every day.
research_analysis.originality_changes: Borrowed: numbered series title, pop-up tallies with sounds, one visible loss, Today's Total and Series Total end card. New: no money appears anywhere; the tally is reels, views and followers; the 'sidekick' is his tripod, named on screen; the setting is a one-person agency day; the finish line is 100K followers by a date.

alex_adaptation.concept: A silent 26-second episode of a numbered series. Alex's working day is scored with pop-ups: +1 for each reel filmed, a real view count, one honest loss, and an end card showing today's followers gained against the series total out of 100,000.
alex_adaptation.target_audience: People who like watching a number go up: build-in-public followers, other creators, and anyone who saw one of his viral Reels.
alex_adaptation.first_frame: Alex at his desk, both fists in the air like he just won something, laptop open. Series title already on screen.

production.editor_instructions: This must be filmed and posted the same day because the end card uses that day's real numbers. Build a reusable template: title, pop-up style (green for plus, red for minus), ding and thud sounds, end card with count-up. Never round the numbers and never skip a day's loss beat. If nothing went wrong that day, the loss is whichever reel got the fewest views, labelled "-1 (flopped)". No voice, no captions other than the ones listed.

testing.promotion_decision: Brand fit 3. Judge this as a series, not a single video: promote the first episode at 48h if follows per 1,000 reached beats the median, and keep making it for 5 episodes before applying the kill rule.
follow_up_variations_if_successful: Client-day episode: the tally counts hooks written, takes filmed and a client's real view count with their permission
Weekend episode: same tally, filmed entirely in the car and at one outdoor spot
Milestone episode at 50K: series total hits halfway, Gary gets a tiny party hat

creative_confidence.score_type: Subjective production-priority score, not predicted viral probability
creative_confidence.rationale: The reference is a 14.1K-subscriber channel at 6.8M views on its fifteenth episode, which is good evidence that a silent scored series can compound. This version is silent like Alex's top Reels and makes the 100K goal a visible, checkable number. The risk is that follower and view counts are less tangible than boxes of product.
uncertainties: Four real numbers are required per episode (episode number, best reel views, followers gained, follower count). This exceeds the usual token limit because the format is a ledger; none are income figures.
Evidence is from YouTube Shorts, not Instagram.
If daily follower gains are small or negative the end card will look bleak. That honesty is part of the format, but he has to be willing to post it.
The forgot-to-record beat should be real when possible; staging it every episode will wear out.
